utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We've been a little delayed because of administrative problems at the Detention Unit, but we are ready to start now. Yes, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Just very briefly. This affects the cross-examination of this witness. Prior to this week, all Defence counsel had been receiving the daily transcript the following day and this week, up until about five minutes ago, we have yet to receive any of the transcripts so, just on behalf of all of Defence counsel, we wanted the record to reflect that we haven't received that as needed and just Your Honours' assistance in the matter from now on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure the registry assistant will deal with that as we are sitting. Thank you for bringing it to the notice of the Chamber. Cross-examination is continuing. Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I wish to say good morning to Your Honours, my learned friends opposite, and the witness, Mr. Izetbegovic. Good morning. At the end of the day yesterday, I intimated the topic that I would address today and that is the issue of the 4th Detachment. As you are aware, yesterday I notified Their Honours that my cross-examination will take another 30 minutes or so, so I should like to appeal to you to assist me in keeping my promise, and you can do so by answering my questions with a "Yes" or "No" or "I don't know." Would you agree with me in saying that the armed forces of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia consisted of the Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 6th of April, 1992, was recognised as an independent state by the members of the European Community?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that Bosnia and Herzegovina was admitted to United Nations membership on the 25th of May, 1992 as the 178th member of the United Nations organisation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I want to ask counsel and the Prosecution, I thought that there were some dates which were agreed on these issues. MR. DI FAZIO: You have. You've taken judicial notice of two dates and I think that's one of the dates. I think it's the 22nd, but I know that you've taken judicial notice of membership of the UN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So counsel can't put those to the witness. They're already on record. The ones taken judicial notice of, if you can check the record, please don't put those issues to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the 4th Detachment was set up by the order of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group of the Yugoslav People's Army on the 5th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said when I learnt about the 4th Detachment. Everything else was guesswork, so I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the 4th Detachment of the JNA was a unit belonging to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that every person in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had military duties?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knew, that should have been so, but I don't know whether it applied to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that every able-bodied person was to do his military service?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct to say that, after completing their military service, all men were transferred to the reserves of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it should have been, but the overall military situation was something I was not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did every person, every man, in his military booklet have an entry indicating the unit he would be assigned to in case of war and mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had one; I don't know about others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that the sending of recruits and care of the reserve forces was carried out by the municipal Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: For as long as it existed. It simply stopped operating because the archives were taken away. The army came and took the archives away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that the Secretariat for National Defence proclaimed mobilisation for the municipality of Bosanski Samac in January 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that members of the detachment belonged to the following ethnic groups: Serbs, that members of the 4th Detachment were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: There were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: That among 4th Detachment members, there were members of the Croatian ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any single case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were there members of the 4th Detachment who were of Yugoslav ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that, among members of the 4th Detachment, there were members of the Macedonian, Albanian, and other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw any such people nor heard of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm and is it true that a large number of Croats and Muslims did not respond to the call-up for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true to say that the reason for failure to respond was the position of the SDA, that members of the Muslim people should not respond to the call-up by the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the Croatian Democratic Community instructed members of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina not to respond to the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot talk about the Croatian Democratic Community, as I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that failure to respond to mobilisation and to military service in those days was a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the rule of law, a state based on the rule of law, which this one no longer was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was the existence of the 4th Detachment publicly announced through the mass media?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the Secretariat for National Defence had the legal authority to requisition material goods for the needs of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly, but again with the approval of the executive council of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the Secretariat for National Defence of Samac municipality, for the needs of the command of the 4th Detachment, requisitioned two premises in the administration building of SIT in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about that, but up until it took over these premises, the 4th Detachment was neither public or legal. It was the personal army of a group of people or one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you please answer my questions. Could you please just tell me whether you know this or not. Do you know that the command of the 4th Detachment was in the SIT building in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe later, after my arrest. I don't know, but I know they asked for that. They wanted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in front of the SIT building, where the command of the 4th Detachment was headquartered, flags were hoisted of the socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was saying, I was arrested and later I had no occasion to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the commander of the 4th Detachment was Radovan Antic, captain first class in reserve?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: De facto, but de jure it was Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the deputy commander was Jovo Savic, reserve captain first class?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that Simo Zaric was reserve sergeant -- reserve corporal, and he was in charge of information and morale?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mehmed Vukovic was operations officer in the detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Miroslav Tadic was assistant commander of the 4th Detachment for logistics?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your indulgence, can I have a couple of minutes to consult with my assistants because there is some problems with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have a problem with translation. The question that Mr. Pisarevic asked is not correctly translated. That's line 5, 6, 7. It says, "And do you know that Simo Zaric was the reserve sergeant?" and the question -- maybe it would be better that Mr. Pisarevic repeats his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Usually it's better. Then we can have it clarified and the interpreters will try to catch him as he speaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Simo Zaric was staff sergeant in reserve and that he was assistant detachment commander for security, information, morale, and notification?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know that on the 1st of April, 1992, a leaflet was published and distributed in town under the heading "List of Domestic Traitors Among the Muslim People in Bosanski Samac"?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that but I don't know who was behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, did you have occasion to see that leaflet?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that on the 2nd of April, 1992, shots were fired at a car when Nizam Ramusovic, Mersad Mesic, and Vitomir Danilo were seriously wounded close to the Mola Cafe owned by Atif Ratic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that. I was in the cafe just then at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Nizam Ramusovic, Mersad Mesic, and Vitomir Danilo were members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now, may I have clarification? Witness, when you answer that you do know that, do you know that now or did you know that at the time when the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was inside, and I was shot at as was the police inspector from MUP Sarajevo. It was an assassination attempt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What I meant -- did you know that Nizam Ramusovic and the other name, Danilo, were members of the 4th Detachment at that time, at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was being said earlier on already that they were over there in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know that the shooting at a passenger vehicle in which Nizam Ramusovic, Mersad Mesic, and Vitomir Danilo were inside ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise. I'm afraid they are not making pauses between questions and answers. Could the question and answer be repeated, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters are complaining about the overlap between the witness and counsel. Can counsel repeat the question, please, and do remember to pause, Mr. Izetbegovic, before you answer so that the interpreters can complete the question, and then you can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, can you confirm that when fire was opened at the passenger car, inside there were Nizam Ramusovic, Mersad Mesic, and Vitomir Danilo, who were members of the 4th Detachment, and that this was done by a reserve police patrol of the police station in Bosanski Samac? Will you please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They just responded to the fire that had been opened previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know who were the members of this reserve police patrol that opened fire at the passenger car in which were Nizam Ramusovic, Mersad Mesic, and Danilo Vitomir?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can verify that through the documents to see who was on duty that night. I don't know who it was, all of those who were among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Will you now answer a few questions for me regarding the formation of the staff of Territorial Defence for Bosanski Samac municipality, which is the next topic I wish to address. Will you tell me, please, how many deputies were there in the municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean from each ethnic group or the total number?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: My question was: How many deputies did the municipal assembly have?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How many deputies in the municipal assembly represented the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think 26. It's a long time ago, sir, but I think it was 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, if you have the numbers, just put it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union, in the parliament which was called the assembly, had 21 deputies?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it had more deputies than the Serb ethnic group, but I don't know the exact number, because there was your party there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action, have two deputy seats in parliament?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the Serbian Democratic Party have 18 deputies in the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago I told you I don't know the figures. I've forgotten them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's a bit embarrassing to say I don't know since I was a member of that parliament. It was a long time ago, so please help me with the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to do.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that the Social Democratic Party had six deputies in the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that the reformist forces, the former Communist Party, had three deputies in the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reformists and that other party, the Liberals, they were smallest. They were no longer parliamentary parties then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Liberals had only one deputy?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. It was Simic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the procedure was prescribed for the nomination of the commander and chief of staff of the municipal command of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: By whom was it prescribed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: By the law. By the law.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see, that's what you mean. Well, most probably yes. That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the proposal for candidates for the post of commander and chief of staff of the municipal staff of Territorial Defence had to be confirmed exclusively by the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm not too well-versed in that procedure, so I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the commander and chief of staff of the TO staff, after nominations had been approved by the municipal assembly, are appointed by the republican command of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it should be, but by then, everything had been disrupted and these institutions no longer existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that the municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac never confirmed Mr. Marko Bozanovic, a reserve captain of the Yugoslav People's Army, as a candidate for the position of TO commander for Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could he be confirmed when the war had started and it never met again?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac never confirmed the candidacy of Mr. Alija Fitozovic, a reserve major of the JNA, for the position of chief of staff of the Territorial Defence staff?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both were nominated together and the nominations sent to the Defence Ministry of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but the war started. This should have gone to the legal authorities, but they no longer existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, can you please let us know when were the nominations put up, a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm coming to those nominations now. These were just preliminary questions regarding preliminary procedures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You see, he's answered your question. He says that, well, there was disruption. So the date is important. He said the war had broken out. So when were the nominations put up?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your question, Your Honour. I will put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, is it correct to say that Mr. Marko Bozanovic, reserve captain of the JNA, was nominated commander of the Territorial Defence staff of Bosanski Samac municipality on the 14th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I think you'll agree with me that on that same day, the 14th of April, 1992, Mr. Alija Fitozovic, reserve major of the Yugoslav People's Army, was nominated as chief of staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both of them in this package of solutions by the Ministry for Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the proposals for the nominations of the staff of Territorial Defence of the Bosanski Samac municipality bypassed legal procedure to the republican staff of Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, sent representatives -- sent by representatives of the Party of Democratic Action and the Croatian Democratic Community of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me at whose proposal did the republican staff or, rather, the commander of the republican staff of Territorial Defence nominate and appoint as commander of the Territorial Defence staff Mr. Marko Bozanovic and as the chief of staff of Territorial Defence Mr. Alija Fitozovic? How did this come about?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the obstructions and everything that was taking place - there had been obstructions for quite some time - I cannot recollect how the proposal was in fact formulated and how it was sent to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're now moving to a different area regarding the local community. Can you tell me, please, whether the fact is correct that the power and authority in the Bosanski Samac local community was in the hands of the representatives of the Party of Democratic Action, the Serbian Democratic Party, and the Croatian Democratic Community?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that at the beginning of April 1992, a coordinating body was set up, the members of which were the representatives of political parties from the Samac municipality who did not take part in governing?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the local community? Yes. Are you thinking about the local community? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I mean, the local community.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what they wanted, to have members in there who were not members of any party, because the local community as a body --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Izetbegovic. You probably didn't understand my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It was a difficult question. I didn't understand it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at the beginning of April 1992, in the local community of Samac, a coordinating body was set up consisting of the representatives of political parties which did not take part in the government of the local community of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As there was inter-party tolerance in town and inter-party cultural intolerance, we wanted to have members from all structures, from non-members from communists, non-communists, and all types of townsfolk to become members of this body because we thought it would function best in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it established or not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was established. Every party, every side had a coordinating body of some kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel and witness, you are not arguing against each other; you are in court. Please wait for the completion of the answers, especially counsel as you seem to be overlapping the answers. Can we have the question and the answer again, please? We have to follow the process of your cross-examination to see whether or not it is dealing with the issues in the indictment. That is why it is important to have a clear answer, completed translation, and a clear question, completed translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best. Thank you for giving me that guidance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on behalf of the Party of Democratic Action, the member of that coordinating body in the local community was Mr. Sulejman Tihic? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you acquainted with the fact that you yourself were not a member of that coordinating body in the local community of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that either. Perhaps I was, perhaps I wasn't, because I was a member of various ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in your statement, you say that you attended a meeting of the coordinating body of the local community of Samac which was held on the 16th of April, 1992. Were you at the meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on that occasion, at that particular meeting which was held on the 16th of April in the local community of the town of Samac, Simo Zaric stated that he was not authorised to transfer the 4th Detachment into the staff of the Territorial Defence of Samac because the 4th Detachment is a unit of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember a statement to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question relates to the 17th of April, 1992, and the events on that date. According to your own testimony, Mr. Izetbegovic, you went into town that morning. You went to the bridge on the River Bosna. Is it true that you went to the park in Bosanski Samac? Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you drove round town in a red car with the mark Yugo of the Kedi type, a Yugo Kedi?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just took the car from Ibol [phoen] and took it -- drove it home because the car belonged to my son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true, Mr. Izetbegovic, that on that particular day, you were carrying a Kalashnikov and a flak jacket?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, on that particular day, see in town members of the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them on that day yet, up until noon when I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Izetbegovic, you were arrested on the 19th of April, 1992 by members of, as you call them, the masked or coloured ones, multicoloured ones but not domestic ones. On that occasion, did they tell you why they were arresting you and on whose orders?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They only said -- that is to say, Laki took a list out of his pocket and looked at it and said, "Ah, you're the golden goose and we're looking for you."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There is a problem with the transcript. The answer was not included of Mr. Izetbegovic. On the question: "You were arrested on the 19th of April, 1992, by members, as you call them, the masked or coloured ones." There isn't an answer but actually it exists. "The multicoloured ones but not the domestic ones." That is the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but it isn't indicated as the answer. Yes. I noticed that. I think they'll correct it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, the witness said "Sareni," meaning multicoloured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it's because the answer is not separated from the question. So I know that they will correct it now that we've pointed it out, yes. Yes. Counsel can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, is it true that those Sareni were in the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: From the 17th of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They personally took me to the police station, Laki and the others, some five or six of them, or ten, in fact. There were ten of them, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that those Sareni acted like policemen?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. They acted like henchmen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they use police competencies and authority?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone, as he saw fit; boots, legs, feet, hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you agree that you were guarded in prison by the police, people wearing police uniforms in fact?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I recognised only two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the police provided security when they took you out to lunch or whenever you left the building, the SUP building for any purpose?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policemen were more afraid of those Sareni than we were ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the chief of police in Bosanski Samac was Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my arrest, I saw him in that capacity for the same -- for the first time, for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Stevan Todorovic commanded the police and the Sareni in the police station of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police, yes. Whether he was in command of the Sareni, I don't know. They know that best themselves how they were assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, are you aware of the fact that Mr. Simo Zaric worked for seven years in the Bosanka company in Bosanski Samac in the capacity of financial director?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Simo Zaric was the chief of police in Bosanski Samac from 1975 to 1979?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that he was director of a company called Buducnost within the composition of the Sipad Sarajevo factory from 1979 to 1982?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't vouch for the dates, but I do know he was there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you acquainted with the fact that from 1982 to 1985 he was the director of the representative offices of the Sipad corporation from Sarajevo in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in Belgrade for a time, but in what capacity and holding what post, I don't know. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at the end of 1985, he got a job in the state security of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that he was there, but I don't remember the year. I can't give you dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. Would you agree that he was the chief of the department of state security with its headquarters in Modrica for the Modrica municipality and the Odzak municipality and Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that that was the person, but when and where, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you also know that he retired on the 1st of September, 1991, after the SDA, HDZ, and SDS came into power?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that he retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Simo Zaric was a well-known cultural and sports figure in the Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which sports?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Just say whether you do know or you don't.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the two of us worked in sports most, but I don't know about Simo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Simo Zaric was a respected citizen of the town and Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, respected or not respected, I can't say. Third parties, a larger audience, will be able to say that about me and him. They must be the ones to give an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Simo Zaric was prominent as a fighter for the idea of Yugoslav-hood?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was. Otherwise, he wouldn't do what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: May we agree that, as a public figure, he very often made public statements and attended citizens' meetings and was in the media a lot?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to notice that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Simo Zaric spoke at a rally on the 15th of February, 1992, in the cinema hall of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that that citizens' rally, on the 15th of February, 1992, was actually held in the cinema of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember the fact that on the 14th of February, 1992, in the Valentino cafe, two young men lost their lives, of Muslim ethnicity, while they were throwing a bomb around?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. That was later established. The manner of death was established later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, I just want to remind you that you've had close to an hour. You've gone beyond the promised time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have one more minute, Your Honour. I've almost finished. It was little difficult to stick to the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you remember that with respect to that, that the rally was held because of that incident that had taken place, that the rally took place in the cinema of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I don't remember a rally of that kind being held. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, I have concluded, but I just have one final question for you. Would you answer it, if you will. Is it true that Fadil Topcagic illegally took your daughter from Bosanski Samac to Belgrade, to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And thank you, Your Honours. I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The next counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and I have a few questions for you. It won't take as long as Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Hopefully.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please take your time. I feel much more comfortable today than I was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, during your testimony yesterday, in answer to questions by the Prosecution when you were speaking about your sojourn in Batajnica, you mentioned some statements linked to events in Bosanski Samac in November 1991 linked to the large exchange between the JNA and the Republic of Croatia. You mentioned that you were involved, that you were part of that exchange. Could you tell me, what was your role in that exchange? Did you represent the official authorities of Bosanski Samac and take part in that procedure?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was the commander of Civil Defence, nominated by the executive council of the municipal assembly, I was proposed by that same executive council to mediate in the exchange. Therefore, I acted as part of my duties. It was mostly an exchange of people from Vukovar and the Croats. And this happened in the harbour of Bosanski Samac. As a citizen, it was my duty to carry out the task assigned to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the exchange took place on the 9th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I took part in three such exchanges. I think it was three. So I cannot recollect the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Those exchanges took place, if I understand you correctly, within the territory of Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the territory of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did other citizens from Bosanski Samac institutions take part in that exchange in one way or another?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were mostly state bodies, and we were attached to them. There was the Red Cross and some other institutions, but some citizens were not prevented from assisting. Some people brought some food or something like that. We didn't make any selection as to whom we would give it to. Whoever put up his hand, we gave it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that the citizens of Bosanski Samac were actively involved in the actual process of exchange and that they were familiar with the method and procedures involved?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The actual method and procedure of exchange was not clear to ordinary citizens. It wasn't even clear to me perhaps. But these things were done spontaneously. People who felt compassion would come. Nothing happened at those exchanges. There were no incidents or anything like that. Both parties looked so awful. These were not soldiers, they were civilians. I remember one wearing pajamas with a plaster cast on. Both sides had members who left one with a very bad impression as you look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in your testimony yesterday and today too, you said that you had been appointed as commander of Civil Defence of Bosanski Samac municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that Civil Defence takes care of first aid to citizens and protects the property of victims and the affected in case of war and natural disasters? That is precisely what you did, is it not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this also implied taking care of the affected and the victims? Can we agree that this implied also extending first aid, medical first aid?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also agree that this implied protection from destruction and devastation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the word "exchange," yesterday in answer to a question from the Prosecution, who also used this term "exchange," and you also said, "I was exchanged in the PTT engineering building in Sarajevo." Can you tell me with whom you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That is precisely why I'm asking you, because you used the word "exchanged" and so did the Prosecution. So would it be right to say that, in fact, you were released?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only term used in those days was "exchange." Of course I was released as soon as I arrived in the area where the other party no longer existed. They had already been separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that you don't know that you were exchanged for somebody specifically?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in the course of your examination-in-chief and also in the cross-examination by my colleague Mr. Pisarevic, you mentioned your meetings with Colonel Nikolic and representatives of the 4th Detachment. You said that you met with them several times, once in Brcko, the second time, I think it was in the building of Bosanski Samac municipality, and once in Obudovac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact number of meetings we had, but we did meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, with representatives of the JNA, specifically with Colonel Nikolic and representatives of the 4th Detachment, did you ever meet with them in the AS Cafe as well?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that any one of your party colleagues or someone else who had contact with the 4th Detachment and the JNA had such a meeting in the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard of it, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in your statement of the 5th of October, you were describing the atmosphere in town immediately prior to the outbreak of conflict. You mentioned that there was unrest in town, that people were taking their children out of town. Does that mean that the town of Bosanski Samac, in that period of time, was being abandoned by entire families or parts of families?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both whole families and parts of families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Does this apply to members of all ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Orthodox and Catholics were the most numerous to leave, but so did the Muslims. Those who were afraid left, but no one was prevented from leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, at the beginning of your testimony, you mentioned that your family was one of the oldest in Bosanski Samac, almost from the very moment the town was founded. In addition to you and your family, were there other respectable families living in Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your relative, Hasan Izetbegovic, who was the former president of Bosanski Samac municipality and director of the veterinary station in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that throughout the duration of the conflict in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, until the signing of the Dayton Agreement, he lived in Bosanski Samac and was director of the veterinary station there?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Ristic was. Maybe later he was. I see Hasan very frequently. We talk about it. I know he experienced a lot of unpleasantness and that he was chased out of his house, as was his brother. We are the children of two brothers and Alija is of the third.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After 1995 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After 1995?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know when they had to leave their own house, that is when they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this was after Dayton or roughly about that time?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how important that is for you, but believe me, I don't know. I don't know exactly. I know that he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that it was after 1994?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please don't insist. I was in Ljubljana then, as I am now, and I haven't seen him since.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the witness did answer that he didn't know the time of departure. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, Madam President, you cannot follow his answers obviously because you don't know B/C/S language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We can follow the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. He said yes, Madam President, that is what I want to say. First he said yes and then that was a problem with the translation and then you didn't get the answer. This gentleman said -- I have at least ten witnesses here. He said exactly yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At which stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At first stage. After the first -- first -- this is 27. This is page 27, line 10. "After 1995?" And he said, "Yes," and then due to these problems with interpretations, he, little bit exchange, changed his position. We hear here, 15 of us, that he said yes. So that's fact. That's a fact, Madam President, and I want the record shows that this witness said, yes, after 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will get that looked at by the audio section.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. That is good approach, audiotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: By the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you so much, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We can get that afterwards. Counsel can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, you had a brother, Safet Izetbegovic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, he's no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, was he a very serious patient during these events and he had to have dialysis treatment?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know that your brother was exchanged in November 1992 and that he left Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that during his stay in Bosanski Samac he was never imprisoned or arrested?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: If such serious patients need to be incarcerated, then I don't know what to say. No, he was not incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I must add, if I may, his wife of is Orthodox faith, and this contributed to his not being arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You think that had something to do with it?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so. One could feel that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in your earlier testimony, you said that you had heard of Hasan Cengic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what positions he held in the Party of Democratic Action in the course of 1991?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that for a time he was Secretary-General of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that Mirsad Ceman was Secretary-General.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since its foundation until the congress we had the other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As a prominent member and official of the SDA in a certain period of time, you frequently attended meetings in the head office, as you mentioned, and Mr. Cengic had proposed and a party decision was adopted on the 15th of February 1991 for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be placed under the control of the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew of anything like that, but if it were so, I wouldn't be at ease with myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Will you -- can you agree with me that, in your view, bearing in mind what you just said, on the 15th of February, 1991, Bosnia and Herzegovina was part of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which was an internationally recognised state?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your executive board in Bosanski Samac, did it receive instructions or information from the head office in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. There had to be some continuity. Someone had to be at the top. And how many of those instructions reached us, how many did not, that's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's 11.00, so I suggest we take a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall take a break and resume at 1130 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination by counsel for Mr. Tadic is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence would now like to introduce a document because we would like to ask the witness some questions pertaining to the document. The document was not disclosed to the Prosecutor previously. It was sent to him for review, but not during the disclosure stage, although it was sent to the Prosecution. The original is in B/C/S, which we have, and there is also an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution confirm that they have seen the document? Or maybe they should look at it first to be sure. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I'd like to look at it first. I have no idea what it is. And whether I'll then be able to confirm that it's been disclosed to us and given to us is something I'm not sure of until I've seen the document. I may not even be able to confirm it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the marshal get the document from counsel and show it to Mr. di Fazio so that he can look at it. MR. DI FAZIO: It looks very familiar. Would Your Honours just bear with me? I believe it has been shown to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can look around. MR. DI FAZIO: I just can't confirm at this stage whether it has or has not been disclosed to us, but it looks very familiar. Perhaps the counsel for the Defence could just continue with his cross-examination in the meantime. I doubt that I'll be objecting to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You won't object? MR. DI FAZIO: No. In fact, I won't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because if there's anything, it will have to wait perhaps. All right. Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number 11/3 and 11/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is titled "Information to All Executive Boards of the SDA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we be correct in this, the registry, please? Is it D11/3? Yes. And D11/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, Your Honour. May I confer with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, would you read through the document, please. Is the document familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am looking at it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what it says in the heading, in the left-hand corner of the document.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says what it says: "To all executive boards of the SDA, Odzak."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The upper part, above that, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Party of Democratic Action," is that what you mean? "Municipal board Odzak."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the date?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read the stamp to be found in the lower right-hand corner of this document?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Party of Democratic Action, SDA, Sarajevo." But these are all copies. Why don't you sometimes show an original?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There will be time for that too. But tell me, do you recognise the signature underneath the stamp?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you remember that in the course of 1991 you received information to put forward candidates as a party, as a party, for a competition for policemen for the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that document, but if the SDA party received this document, then the same document must have been sent to the SDS party and HDZ party to fill them in -- to fill the vacancies in, according to electoral procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From the SDA headquarters?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The MUP would send out documents of this kind to the parties that had been in the parliamentary elections. That means a legal institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, you will agree with me when I say that the police force in countries all over the world protects the state and not party interests and that it is not up to -- and that party affiliation must not be criteria for admission into the Ministry of Internal Affairs. You would agree with me there, would you not? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: How come that in Samac, then, most of the policemen were representatives of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please just try and answer my question. Yes or no. Do you agree with my assertion or not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Izetbegovic, you mentioned in your previous testimony that you heard about the -- had heard about the Patriotic League; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just that I had heard of it, yes. But don't ask me who I heard this from because that will lead to a general mix-up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I won't. I won't be asking you that. Have you heard of Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. He's a guest here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you read his book "Sly Strategy"?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not read his book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever at a meeting of any kind, a party meeting or some other meeting in Sarajevo with Mr. Sefer Halilovic at which military matters were discussed, armament for the Democratic Action Party and similar topics?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Izetbegovic, just a few more questions to go back to the exchange, to your exchange, as you refer to it. When you were exchanged, at the time in Sarajevo, were the representatives of the International Community or the Red Cross present? The International Red Cross, I mean.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not notice the Red Cross, but the International Community did do the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you were exchanged in Bosanski -- during the exchange in Bosanski Samac where you took part between the Yugoslav People's Army and the Republic of Croatia, were the representatives of the International Red Cross and the International Community present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were, both parts, the International Red Cross, Krst and Kriz, and the International Community as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And just a slight clarification, Mr. Izetbegovic, not linked to any of these topics, the ones that we've just discussed. During your testimony on the 5th of October, 2001, when you described your arrest and the torture that you had to endure by the, as you term them, Sareni, you said the following: "When we reached the SUP building, Laki came up to me and said ..."

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall continue you and tell you what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, for procedure.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I want to say it for truth, because of the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You wait for counsel to complete his question, and if he's quoting what he says he said, he must be quoting from the transcript. So you don't have to correct him. You wait for the answer. If the quotation is not correct according to you, then you say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat. "When we reached the SUP building, Laki came up to me and said, If you let one sound out of your mouth, a single word, `If you say a single word about what we did to you, I'll kill you with my own hands.'" Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What did you think? Whom weren't you allowed to say anything to? You mean the people taking you off? What was your understanding of that?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think he meant the people taking me but if anybody ever were to ask me how it was, that I wasn't allowed to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the authorities?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Izetbegovic, I have no further questions for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The next counsel to cross-examine. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Slobodan Zecevic, an attorney, and I will be asking you a few questions. Mr. Izetbegovic, after the elections, the multiparty elections that were held in November 1990, you were in them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the time, you were elected or nominated the vice-president of the executive council of the Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Executive board, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Executive board. You took over your duties sometime in January 1991, did you not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was January. January or February, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you remained in that post until April 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, on page 2141, line 10 -- lines 10 and 11 of the transcript of the 3rd of October, in answer to a question put by the Prosecutor relating to your involvement in the SDA party, you stated: "After that, I joined the municipal structures and handed over my duties to another person, Mr. Sulejman Tihic, that was in the party. I remained the vice-president of the party, and he was the president of the party. I was very busy in the municipal assembly, and I was not able to perform both functions." Is it true that that is the statement you made?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Izetbegovic, the duties that prevented you from performing both functions, that is to say, in the party and in the municipality, related to the duties that you had as vice-president of the executive board of the municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The executive board of the municipality dealt with the daily affairs of the municipality, the needs -- daily needs and requirements of the municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it dealt with the utilities, the electricity, the sewage system, things like that?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the complete infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the electricity board, power supply?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samac was a big building site, and the overall infrastructure was being reconstructed, in fact, and this was nearing its close, but it was my duty to contact the different firms and to enable financial resources for the realisation and implementation of that reconstruction plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What construction site? What type of construction?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: We changed the whole infrastructure and laid down a new infrastructure and asphalted the roads and sorted the town planning in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the infrastructure," do you mean electric cables -- just let me finish, please, if you will. Do you mean telephone cables, electrical cables, remote heating systems, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Izetbegovic: Within the frameworks of your competencies and duties, that is to say, of the executive board, health comes under those competencies too, does it not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Primary health protection?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primary health protection too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And secondary health protection?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, secondary health protection too, but primary first of all, and certain individuals were in charge of primary health care within the field -- within the health department, as is customary. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify one point. Health protection is within the framework of the competencies of the executive board of the municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the whole of life, the life of the people, is under the assembly and the executive board, because the executive board just had executive powers, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "primary health care" or "health protection," you mean the health centres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when you talk about secondary, you are referring to hospitals and similar institutions?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please: Within the frameworks of your duties, you also had the heating or remote heating from the power plant, heating power plant, under you?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but nobody paid anybody, actually, for these services.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you to mean that this was one of your duties and that you had a great deal of problems?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were enormous problems, because it was always difficult to balance the accounts and come by the necessary resources needed and the fuel needed for the heating system.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Izetbegovic: Within the frameworks of the competencies of the executive board of the municipality were social welfare matters as well?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are always present, at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that a serious part of your duties? What I mean is, did it take up -- did social welfare and the social services take up a great deal of your time?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't my main line of action, but I did contact individuals and groups for social assistance and so on, and then we would react, but there wasn't actually a programme for social welfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There was a centre for social welfare, was there not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a centre for social welfare. Now, how far it was able to act or what it was able to do, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The centre informed the executive board of the municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what it should have done. I don't know how frequently the reports were sent in to us, but usually the representative of the social welfare centre would be present, would attend meetings when we would discuss the materials sent in to us and the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The centre for social work and welfare also dealt with the question of unemployment, social dues and grants and things like that?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the social expenditures and benefits were given generally to people who had really reached the dregs, alcoholics, and who had nobody to look after them. As for employment, there wasn't that much unemployment in Samac. Everybody did something. And then the private businesses started to emerge. So this was not a burning question, unemployment, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Within the frameworks of your competencies, did you have housing under you? Was housing a part of your area?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a separate department to deal with housing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I say "your competencies and authorisations," I'm always referring to you as the executive organ of the executive board. Did it deal with housing and housing problems?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes, if somebody would come to the executive board for assistance, for a flat, if they wanted to get an apartment or something like that, then it would, but not officially, and it was not the only body.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about town planning, urban development and construction in the town? Did that come under the executive board?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the executive board was the coordinator for all institutions, and you said a moment ago we had what we call the SIZ, the interest communities, so they did that. And there was a SIZ, an S-I-Z, for housing policy. The executive board was just an overall body to supervise it. Now, how far it did supervise and coordinate, I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The interest communities, the SIZ organisations that you mentioned, they were responsible for their work to the executive board, were they not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: They should have been, yes, but they all gained quite a bit of independence and autonomy and nobody listened to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, Mr. Izetbegovic, in answer to a question put to you, you said that on the 23rd of March, 1992, you were in Sarajevo to discuss budgetary matters.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The budget of the municipality also came under the competencies of the executive board, a draft budget, a proposal for the budget that is then handed up to the assembly for a final ruling?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday during your testimony -- that is to say, you mentioned that the closing of the bridge was another matter under your competence.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that traffic was another area which came under the auspices, so to speak, of the executive board of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all this is linked together. The executive board had to react from time to time, without having to wait for the assembly to make a decision, because it was -- everything was in a critical state. There were burning issues, masses of them at the same time, and there was an enormous bottleneck that had been created on the bridge, and the Croats would let traffic pass by when they felt like it. So I wanted to see that this enormous amount of transport and this bottleneck in Samac could be relieved in some way and passage to be ensured.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The executive board was responsible to the assembly, of course, for its work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is the body that nominated it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I want to ask you something else, Mr. Izetbegovic, another area. You are testifying before this -- you've been testifying before this Tribunal since the beginning of October; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you staying at the Bel Air Hotel, Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC: [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I should answer questions of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Don't answer. Where are we going?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, actually, Your Honours, we have raised this matter a couple of days ago, I mean before the recess, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in our opinion, this goes directly in the issue of the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And according to the questions which I am about to pose, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
